name: L'Hombre
description: L'Hombre (Spanish for 'The Man') is a historical three-player card game that was the most popular and prestigious card game in Europe for over two centuries (c. 1650-1850). Played with a 40-card Spanish-suited (or standard) deck, it introduced the revolutionary concept of bidding to determine the trump suit and the 'declarer' (The Hombre) who plays alone against the other two. It is the direct ancestor of games like Ombre, Quadrille, and Skat.

history.origins: Developed in Spain in the early 17th century. It was a courtly game, widely mentioned in classical literature (e.g., Cervantes, Pope).
timeline: 1660s: Becomes the sensation of the English and French royal courts.
1750s: Peak popularity across Europe as 'The game of the nobility'.
1850s: Replaced by Whist and later Bridge, though it survives in Denmark and Spain today.
history.cultural: Famously described in Alexander Pope's poem 'The Rape of the Lock'. In Denmark, it is still played competitively by the 'L'Hombre-Klub'.
history.evolution: The game's 'Matadors' system (permanent trumps) inspired the higher-rank systems in later games like Spades and Belote.

setup.players: 3 players (The Hombre plays against the other two).
setup.deck: 40 cards. 8s, 9s, 10s removed. Rank (Non-trump): K, Q, J, 7-2, A (in black suits) or 2-4, K, Q, J, A (in red suits).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards. 13 cards form a talon (Pila).

rules.objective: Win more tricks than either of the other two players individually.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit if possible.
2. Highest Matador wins any trick, followed by other trumps, then high cards of led suit.
3. **Puesta**: If the Hombre doesn't win more tricks than one opponent, they 'lose' and must pay the pot.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if void, may play any card.
In game contracts, Spadille (A of spades) and Basta (A of clubs) are permanent trumps; Manille is second highest (2 in black trumps, 7 in red).
Matadors have limited follow-suit exemptions: when a trump is led, you need not play a matador unless a higher matador was led and you have no other trumps.
Declarer wins by taking more tricks than either defender; nolo contracts: declarer must take no tricks.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Spadille. If you hold the Ace of Spades, you have a 90% chance of winning your first lead. Use it to 'flush' the opponents' trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Evaluation: Only bid 'Solo' if you hold at least two of the three top Matadors and four other trumps. In a 3-player game, card density is high, so a single missing Matador can be fatal.
strategy.advanced: The Defensive Pinch: As the two defenders against the Hombre, you must cooperate. If you have the lead and know your partner has no trumps left, lead a suit where the Hombre is likely weak to force them to use a high Matador early.
tips: Remember the 'Manille' changes depending on the trump suit! In Diamonds, it is the 2; in Spades, it is the 7.
If the Hombre takes cards from the Talon, watch which cards they discard. It tells you exactly which suits they are void in.

variations.name: Grand
variations.description: Only Spadille and Basta count as trumps. Both declarer and defenders exchange with the talon. Declarer must exchange at least five cards; win requires at least five tricks. Rated like Grand Tourné or Simple Nolo.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes contract and exchange rules only; no engine constant overrides in source.

variations.name: Grandissimo
variations.description: Like Grand but declarer does not exchange any cards; to Grand what Solo is to Simple Game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation differs from Grand only by declarer exchange; no engine overrides documented.

variations.name: Bonus for first five tricks
variations.description: Declarer may declare intent to take the first five tricks before playing to the first trick. Success scores an extra token; failure loses one token to each player. Outcome is independent of the contract result.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional bonus scoring only; no engine constant overrides in source.
